newsitem.title: GERMANY: Arson arrests cast shadow over German village.
newsitem.headline: Arson arrests cast shadow over German village.

text.p: Prosecutors have arrested a fourth resident of the tiny German village of Dolgenbrodt as a suspect in the 1992 firebombing of a foreigners' hostel.

The arrests have thrown the spotlight back on the village of 260 people south of Berlin where press reports have suggested a widespread conspiracy lay behind the destruction of a new hostel the day before 86 asylum-seekers were to move in.
Frankfurt-on-the-Oder prosecutor Petra Marx said on Friday the new suspect, identified as "Hans S", was the stepfather of "Marco S", who was arrested previously.

They are accused of providing the firebombs. Two other villagers are accused of employing right-wing thugs to use them in an attack which took place during a wave of racist and neo-Nazi violence after German unification.

"I think the motives lay in the fact that some in Dolgenbrodt feared for the welfare of their children, their homes and their property and were willing to pay any price to stop the hostel," Marx said.
A young right-winger was convicted last year of setting the fire but no connection was proved to inhabitants of the village, where many Berliners have weekend retreats.
Although no one was injured, the fire caused 300,000 marks ($195,000) of damage.
Ute Preissler, the mayor at the time of the fire, told Reuters on Thursday that although most villagers had been against the hostel, they had not supported arson.
"We tried at that time to use legal means to stop the construction," Preissler said. "But I would in no way say that that was a call to commit a firebombing."

Local florist Thomas O. was arrested this month and prosecutors accuse him of hiring the arsonist or arsonists for 2,000 marks to start the fire and, if caught, keep quiet about who had commissioned the attack.
A 48-year-old master electrician, Gerd G., was arrested on Wednesday on suspicion of having provided the money.

A young right-winger named Silvio Jackowski, 19 at the time of the blaze, was found guilty last year of starting the fire for racist motives. He received a suspended sentence of two years, having already spent 11 months in investigative custody.
